brief: Wells Fargo raises its Q4/Q4 core PCE forecast to 3.2% (from 3.1%) on incoming BEA methodology changes, noting stubbornly high PCE inflation drove the FOMC's September 16 hike; it expects one more Fed hike this year, lifting its fed funds forecast to 4.00-4.25% by year-end 2026 with no change in 2027, arguing further hikes are hard to justify once inflation is supply-driven and the labor market is not overheating. Q3 GDP is forecast at 3.0% annualized, a downgrade mostly reflecting a wider net exports drag (nearly 2pp), even as AI-driven investment keeps propelling growth, though its incremental boost should shrink as it matures; no outright investment decline is expected. August payrolls and a 1.2% retail sales rebound cut labor-market downside risk and lifted the Q3 PCE forecast to 3.2%, but payroll growth is seen moderating to ~65K/month and unemployment edging up to 4.2% by year-end. A higher floor under long-term yields (growth, issuance, policy uncertainty) lifts the 10-year forecast to 4.90%/4.75% and pressures housing and mortgage rates, now above 7%. This year's deficit is forecast at $2.1 trillion (~6.5% of GDP). Globally, Wells Fargo now expects more advanced-economy tightening (BoJ, ECB, possibly BoE, RBA) even as PBoC eases, while upgrading 2026 global GDP to 2.9% and global CPI to 4.4%.
